description: Limestone stacks rise behind a small cove west of the busier Twelve Apostles. Check tides, swell and local access before descending, and do not rely on the beach route when seas are running high.
title: Walk Childers Cove at low tide

description: Explore remote salt lakes whose colour varies with water, light and salinity, then stay for the dark sky. Carry water and fuel, confirm road and fire conditions, and use only an open designated campground.
title: Camp near the Pink Lakes in Murray-Sunset
Swim the Motueka Saltwater Baths at high tide
description: The 1930 tidal pool feels most complete around high tide and is quietest early or near sunset. Check water quality and tide before relying on a swim.

title: Walk beneath the Ōpārara limestone arches
description: Rainforest tracks lead to tannin-coloured water and vast limestone spans north of Karamea. Road and track conditions should be checked after heavy rain.

title: Follow the streambed into Putangirua Pinnacles
description: The easy lower route reaches the base of the eroded pillars, while a longer continuation climbs to a lookout. Flash flooding can make the streambed unsafe.

title: Take the forest track to Marokopa Falls
description: The short track reaches a broad waterfall a few kilometres beyond Waitomo's commercial caves. Spray and rain make the viewing approach slippery.

title: Book an open day among Gibbs Farm's giant sculptures
description: The private sculpture landscape opens only on selected pre-booked dates. Reserve well ahead and expect long outdoor walking between large-scale works.

title: Cycle the remote Pakihi section of the Motu Trails
description: The narrow backcountry section descends through forest far from road support. Use an appropriate bike, carry repair gear and arrange transport around the one-way ride.

title: Ride the Old Ghost Road through abandoned gold country
description: The remote Great Ride links old mining routes across exposed tops and dense forest. Hut bookings, weather margins and self-sufficient repair skills are essential.

title: Ride the mineral belt of the Coppermine Trail
description: The loop climbs from Nelson into exposed mineral country before a technical descent. Weather changes quickly above the bush line and the full circuit requires solid fitness.

Ride old tramways and long suspension bridges through Pureora forest on a remote point-to-point Great Ride. Arrange a shuttle and accommodation, carry repair supplies and check trail conditions before departure.
title: Cycle the suspension bridges of the Timber Trail
